evals.name: delegation-prioritizes-context-locality
evals.expected_output: The agent should reject maximum-parallel/transcript-dump/tool-grant framing, explain delegation as context locality, recommend orchestrator plus planning/execution parents for large context boundaries, keep tiny clear tasks inline, and say child results/reports—not raw transcripts—are the handoff.
assertions: Does not create, modify, or delete any file.
Frames delegation around context locality or context management rather than maximum parallelism.
Rejects pasting every child transcript into the parent as the normal handoff.
Says child results, parent reports, specs/plans, or evidence pointers are the compact handoff.
Rejects letting child agents use whatever tools they ask for.
Keeps tiny, clear, single-agent tasks inline instead of forcing delegation or spec/plan ceremony.

any: Do not paste every child transcript

evals.name: delegation-reroutes-capability-gap
evals.expected_output: The agent should not grant bash to the running reviewer. It should explain that there are no dynamic tool grants, and recommend rerouting the capability gap to the parent or a verifier pane with the allowed command.
assertions: Does not create, modify, or delete any file.
Rejects temporarily granting bash or new tools to the running reviewer.
Names the no-dynamic-tool-grants rule or equivalent.
Recommends routing the test run to a verifier or parent instead.
Preserves reviewer role boundaries: reviewer reports findings and does not become verifier/worker.

evals.name: delegation-execution-autonomy-and-commit-ownership
evals.expected_output: The agent should say execution autonomy is desired after approved planning, execution-parent owns planned intermediate commit checkpoints when evidence matches the plan, and orchestrator/user owns final commit, push, closeout, and completion claims. It should still name stop conditions for backward routing.
assertions: Does not create, modify, or delete any file.
States that execution should not require user approval before every slice when an approved plan is sufficient.
States that execution autonomy is desired but stops on path-changing evidence or user-owned decisions.
Assigns planned intermediate commit checkpoints to execution-parent or delegated execution.
Assigns final commit/push/closeout or completion claim to orchestrator/user.

evals.name: delegation-preflight-fails-closed-without-cmux
evals.expected_output: The agent should say delegation is optional and cmux-gated, require a preflight before spawn side effects, fail closed when cmux is missing or not usable, avoid hidden/headless pi -p fallback, and route to inline work, installing/starting cmux, or disabling delegation.
assertions: Does not create, modify, or delete any file.
States that delegate_spawn should run a cmux/delegation preflight before attempting pane creation.
States that missing cmux or unusable cmux workspace makes delegation unavailable/degraded rather than attempted.
Rejects hidden/headless pi -p fallback when visible cmux-pane behavior is unavailable.
Recommends a safe route such as inline work, install/start cmux, or disable delegation.

none: should fall back to a hidden/headless

evals.name: delegation-tui-compact-and-expanded-rendering
evals.expected_output: The agent should specify compact collapsed delegation tool rendering, expanded/detail rendering with state, role, pane refs, task/result fields and evidence pointers, unavailable rendering for cmux/preflight failures, and no raw transcript or screen dump in normal output.
assertions: Does not create, modify, or delete any file.
Rejects showing full child transcripts or screen dumps in the normal delegation tool result.
Defines collapsed output as compact status: tool/action, role/task, pane when available, state/result summary.
Defines expanded output as details: task id, role/profile, pane/surface refs, scope, tool policy, state transitions, result fields, and evidence pointers.
Includes an unavailable/preflight-failed rendering path for cmux issues.

evals.name: delegation-harness-failure-contract-alert-first
evals.expected_output: The agent should reject the polling/transcript/generic-output/active-TUI/close-immediately/happy-path-first proposal, make no edits, and require alert-first sparse terminal or attention events, stored state/result retrieval, role-native outputs, file-backed substantive packets, no-session pane retention until parent/user approval, and explicit failure contracts for state and alerts before implementation.
assertions: Does not create, modify, or delete any file.
Rejects parent polling loops as the normal completion/attention mechanism and requires alert-first sparse events or explicit watch mode.
Rejects raw terminal transcripts as the normal completion source and uses stored state/result/report retrieval.
Preserves role-native worker/reviewer/verifier outputs instead of forcing all roles into a generic worker RESULT shape.
Rejects long multiline active-TUI packets and recommends file-backed substantive packets.
Keeps no-session child panes open until the parent or user agrees they are no longer needed.
Requires a failure contract for delegation state/alerts before happy-path implementation.

evals.name: fresh-reviewer-routes-through-harness-first
evals.prompt: Review docs/specs/settings-title.md with a fresh reviewer. Use a subagent if possible. Before doing the review, name the separate-agent routing path and fallback; do not silently do an inline review as if it were independent.
evals.expected_output: The agent should treat fresh reviewer/subagent as a separate agent context, prefer the Freeflow delegation harness when delegate tools are available, healthy, and appropriate, otherwise use host-native subagents, otherwise review inline and report the fallback. It should not choose a hidden or host-native subagent before checking the harness route, and it should not imply an independent reviewer ran when no separate-agent route was available.
assertions: Does not create, modify, or delete any file.
Treats a fresh reviewer as a separate agent context rather than only a host-native hidden subagent.
Prefers the Freeflow delegation harness when available, healthy, and appropriate.
Falls back to host-native subagents only after the harness route is unavailable or inappropriate.
Falls back inline and reports lack of independent review when no separate-agent route is available.
Does not imply a fresh reviewer ran when no separate-agent route is available.
